title: ticfac run <epic>: one command starts, resumes and attaches, with no flags, env or paths
description: The friction list in 2jn's description. 'ticfac run <epic>' replaces 'GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) nohup ticfac run-epic -profiles <path> -wall 86400 <epic> &'. It starts the run in the background (detached, surviving the terminal) and attaches the live view (89m); Ctrl-C detaches, it never stops the run. Running it again on a live run attaches; on a stopped run it resumes. It accepts the epic id everywhere (the run id epic-<id> stays the internal identity). It fetches the GitHub token from gh auth token when, and only when, the repo's close-out rule needs a forge, and says so. It detects a live herdr (socket) and dispatches into herdr panes using an EMBEDDED profile set (no filesystem path; --no-herdr opts out, --profiles stays as an expert override). There is no wall-clock default: liveness belongs to b1t, and the -wall bound becomes an opt-in backstop. run-epic stays as an alias for scripts.

acceptance_criteria: 'ticfac run <epic>' in a repo with herdr running starts an epic in herdr panes with no flag, env var or path; a second invocation attaches, and on a stopped run resumes; Ctrl-C detaches without stopping; the token is fetched from gh only when the close-out needs it; run-epic still works; tests cover detach/attach/resume and the herdr detection
